name: Seated Neck Release
description: Slow, mindful lateral neck stretch that melts away cervical spine tension accumulated from hours of looking down at laptops and lecture slides.
alignmentCues: Sit tall with your feet flat on the floor and spine erect.
Gently drop your right ear toward your right shoulder without lifting the shoulder.
Place your right hand softly over your left ear without pulling—let gravity do the work.
Hold for 5 slow breaths, release, and repeat on the left side.
breathingCue: Inhale to lengthen your spine, exhale to release side neck tightness.
studyBenefit: Relieves tension headaches and reduces forward head posture strain.
contraindications: Avoid if experiencing acute cervical herniation or sharp neck pain.

name: Seated Spinal Twist
description: Gentle rotational twist using your desk chair to restore thoracic mobility and encourage natural spinal disc hydration during long study sessions.
alignmentCues: Sit sideways on your chair or centered with feet planted hip-width apart.
Inhale deeply to lift the crown of your head upward.
Exhale and twist gently toward the right, holding the backrest with both hands.
Keep both sit bones equally grounded and gaze softly over your right shoulder.
Hold for 5 deep breaths, then switch to the left side.
breathingCue: Inhale to find vertical length; exhale to rinse out muscular tension.
studyBenefit: Eases lower back stiffness and aids digestion slowed by sedentary sitting.
contraindications: Twist gently without forcing; avoid deep twists if experiencing acute disc injury.

name: Seated Cat-Cow Stretch
description: A dynamic spinal flexion and extension rhythm that synchronizes movement with breath to re-energize a sluggish, desk-bound body.
alignmentCues: Place both hands firmly on your knees with feet grounded.
Cow: Inhale, arch your back forward, lift your chest, and gaze gently toward the ceiling.
Cat: Exhale, round your spine backward, tuck your chin to your chest, and draw your navel in.
Flow smoothly between both states for 6 to 8 complete breath cycles.
breathingCue: Inhale on the heart-opening arch; exhale on the rounding back expansion.
studyBenefit: Improves spinal circulation and breaks up mental grogginess immediately.
contraindications: Keep movement within a comfortable, pain-free range.

name: Wrist & Finger Decompressor
description: Targeted forearm extensor and flexor release that counters repetitive typing fatigue, trackpad strain, and pen-gripping tension.
alignmentCues: Extend your right arm straight in front of you at shoulder height with palm facing forward.
Use your left hand to gently draw your right fingertips backward toward your forearm.
Hold for 15 seconds, feeling a gentle stretch through the inner wrist and palm.
Flip the hand so fingers point downward and palm faces your chest; gently press back.
Rotate both wrists in circles 5 times each way, then repeat with the left hand.
breathingCue: Keep breathing steadily through your nose while softening shoulder muscles.
studyBenefit: Prevents repetitive strain injuries and relieves cramping from handwritten exams.
contraindications: Never pull aggressively on finger joints; ease off if tingling occurs.

name: Seated Eagle Arms
description: Deep rhomboid and shoulder stretch that broadens the space between your shoulder blades where stress and hunching concentrate.
alignmentCues: Bring both arms out in front at 90-degree angles to your body.
Cross your right elbow under your left elbow; wrap forearms and press palms together.
(If palms do not touch, hold opposite shoulders like a hug).
Gently lift your elbows to shoulder level while keeping shoulders down away from ears.
Hold for 4 full breaths, unwind, and switch arms with left under right.
breathingCue: Send your breath directly into the space between your shoulder blades.
studyBenefit: Unlocks persistent upper-back knots caused by hunching over a keyboard.
contraindications: Modify to a shoulder-hug variation if suffering from acute rotator cuff soreness.

name: Seated Forward Fold
description: A restorative calming inversion done seated that cools down an overstimulated brain and gently lengthens the lumbar spine.
alignmentCues: Sit near the front edge of your chair with feet wider than hip-width apart.
Rest hands on thighs, take a slow deep inhale, and lengthen your spine.
Exhale and hinge from your hips, lowering your torso between or onto your thighs.
Let your arms hang heavily toward the floor and relax your neck completely.
Breathe softly for 6 slow breaths, then roll up one vertebra at a time.
breathingCue: Exhale with a gentle sigh to trigger the parasympathetic rest response.
studyBenefit: Relieves lower back compression and promotes blood circulation to the brain.
contraindications: Avoid hanging head below hips if prone to dizziness or high blood pressure.

name: Chair Pigeon / Figure-4
description: Opens tight outer hips and the piriformis muscle that tighten severely during prolonged sitting in library carrels.
alignmentCues: Sit with both feet grounded and back away from the backrest.
Lift your right ankle and cross it over your left knee, creating a number 4 shape.
Flex your right foot actively to protect your right knee joint.
Sit tall; if you need more sensation, hinge gently forward from your hips with a flat back.
Hold for 5 deep breaths, uncross carefully, and switch to the left leg.
breathingCue: Exhale slowly into any tight sensations in your outer hip.
studyBenefit: Prevents sciatica, reduces lower back aches, and releases emotional stress stored in hips.
contraindications: Do not push down directly on the knee; back off if knee twinges.

name: Overhead Crescent Side Stretch
description: Expands the ribcage and intercostal muscles, creating immediate physical space for deeper, fuller breathing when feeling anxious.
alignmentCues: Sit upright with feet anchored and interlace your fingers overhead, palms pressed upwards.
Inhale to grow tall through your spine.
Exhale and gently lean your upper body to the right, keeping both sit bones rooted.
Gaze forward or slightly upward under your left arm.
Hold for 3 deep breaths, return to center on an inhale, and repeat on the left.
breathingCue: Feel your ribs fan open like an accordion as you breathe into the elongated side.
studyBenefit: Counters shallow chest breathing common during high-stress exam cramming.
contraindications: Keep arms at shoulder height if overhead extension causes shoulder impingement.

name: Seated Chest Opener & Shoulder Rolls
description: Counters the rounded-shoulder 'student posture' by gently expanding the pectorals and stimulating open, confident posture.
alignmentCues: Scoot toward the front of your chair with feet planted firmly.
Interlace your fingers behind your lower back, or hold the sides of the chair seat.
Roll your shoulders up, back, and down away from your ears.
Gently squeeze your shoulder blades together and lift your sternum upward.
Take 4 slow, expansive chest breaths, feeling renewed oxygenation.
breathingCue: Fill your lungs completely from belly to collarbones on every inhale.
studyBenefit: Immediately boosts alertness and combats midday study fatigue and slumping.

name: Desk Rest / Chair Child's Pose
description: A deeply restorative mini-retreat at your study desk that darkens the eyes, quiets cognitive chatter, and resets your nervous system.
alignmentCues: Clear a small space on your desk and fold your forearms together on the desk surface.
Slide your chair back slightly so your torso can fold forward comfortably.
Rest your forehead softly on your stacked forearms or hands.
Close your eyes and release all tension in your jaw, tongue, and eyelids.
Surrender to slow, natural nasal breathing for 1 to 2 minutes.
breathingCue: Let every exhale wash away exam worry and mental chatter.
studyBenefit: Gives eyes complete relief from blue light screen glare and resets focus.
contraindications: Ensure your desk is stable and comfortable to lean upon.
